basics.name: Robert DeRose
basics.label: Systems & Platform Engineering | Embedded Linux & IoT
basics.summary:
I build software that bridges hardware and the cloud: embedded Linux, IoT device management, mesh messaging, and the CI/CD to ship it. Shipping code since 2010 in Python, Java, Elixir, Go, Rust, TypeScript, and Nix: the right tool for each job.

For 3 years I've been the lead engineer for SFERO, Checkpoint's best-selling new product, with large deployments worldwide, and for the CI/CD the whole company ships on. Since 2025 I've worked agent-first with models from Anthropic and OpenAI, using spec-driven development and Beads. Working this way, I made a ~64K-line custom DDS messaging prototype unnecessary by packaging Zenoh with an MQTT bridge in ~2 weeks.

work.name: Checkpoint Systems
work.summary: Lead engineer for SFERO, Checkpoint's best-selling new product, since 2023, with large deployments worldwide.
highlights: Replaced a multicast-based messaging proof of concept, ~64K lines of custom Data Distribution Service (DDS) code built over 5 months, with a packaged Zenoh/MQTT platform in ~2 weeks: added mutual TLS (mTLS) across the device fleet, adapted its per-application leader election, and built a React operator console

Rewrote every device UI as React 19 and PatternFly 6 modules on Vite with custom mise tooling, replacing Cockpit modules built from raw HTML and JavaScript that drove Bash scripts; consolidated overlapping modules, updated the Copier templates to match, and packaged a customized Cockpit build with Entra ID sign-in built in; migrated Flask dashboards into Cockpit, removing ~77K lines of legacy code

Rebuilt the provisioning app in Rust/Tauri, now used by every approved employee and contractor: a server secured with Microsoft Entra ID gives the app the device credentials it needs to automate setup, and those secrets stay in the macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager

Introduced AI-assisted development across the team's repositories: spec-driven development with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex), Beads for task tracking and agent memory, and gated code review, taking the team from delegating small agent tasks to delivering whole projects with agents

As a spare-time side project, prototyped an Elixir/OTP successor to our RFID loss-prevention platform, with restart-safe alarm processing that never replays an alarm, and alarm strategies that operators change in the UI, or integrators change through APIs, without new code

Set the company's packaging and release standard: built and operate the shared CI/CD the whole company relies on, adopted by 30+ repositories in 3 global offices. Its reusable GitHub Actions run on a custom, spec-tested Bash framework that builds and tests Debian packages for Python, Rust, TypeScript, and generic projects on arm64 and amd64, across all three supported Ubuntu LTS releases

Rebuilt the company's custom APT repository server, replacing hours-long cron-driven index rebuilds with filesystem watchers and a cached package index: packages now publish within a minute, concurrent publishing is safe, and build-and-test cycles dropped from hours to minutes

Built a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner platform with ephemeral runners: builds run 10x faster and are reproducible, because no build can quietly depend on packages another pipeline left behind; runners self-update weekly and share a Debian caching proxy

As lead engineer, redesigned the device OS support packages from the ground up around Linux standards instead of home-grown conventions: product-independent Debian packages, monorepo support in the shared CI/CD, and ~44K fewer lines of legacy code; led EN 18031 security hardening across authentication, SSH access, and rate limiting
Strengthened device security by replacing custom privilege handling with standard sudo rules, polkit, and Cockpit's native APIs, so each role can run only the actions it needs
Added OpenID Connect (OIDC) sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID to the device UIs, giving each person an individual company account with role-based access

Led development of a Python service for provisioning, monitoring, and updating networked RFID and electronic article surveillance (EAS) readers; added support for three hardware families and over-the-air (OTA) firmware updates over MQTT

Automated builds of CPython 3.11–3.15 Debian packages tuned with profile-guided optimization (PGO) and link-time optimization (LTO) for three Ubuntu LTS releases, standardizing Python across product lines
Built a cross-platform device provisioning app in Python/Flet that configures devices offline over SSH

Made the standard the default: reusable Copier project templates give every new project the shared CI/CD, Debian packaging, and UI tooling from day one, including the REST service template behind Checkpoint's Readfinity Core RFID reader software
printHighlights: Replaced a 5-month, ~64K-line DDS prototype with Zenoh/MQTT in 2 weeks

Cut APT repository publishing from hours to under a minute

Built a Rust/Tauri provisioning app used by all approved staff and contractors

work.name: Edmunds GovTech
highlights: Built an automated upgrade system that took government customers straight from several major versions behind to the latest release, instead of one version at a time, saving technicians hours to days per upgrade
Designed the upgrade system's database migration engine for MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and Actian Zen (PSQL), absorbing years of schema changes previously tracked by hand in Excel
Led a team of three developers integrating Orbeon Forms into the product
Built a JavaFX application to install and manage the product's Windows services
Moved the entire codebase from System.out.println to Apache Log4j 2 with a script that analyzed each call's context
Migrated all source code from Subversion to Git and set up GitLab CI/CD
printHighlights: Built one-step upgrades across major versions, saving techs hours to days

work.name: Linode, Inc.
highlights: Personally built Linode's OAuth 2.0 platform, integrating the legacy ColdFusion website and the new Python API service: single sign-on (SSO) for Linode's apps, an OAuth provider for third-party apps, and a custom SSH PAM module that authenticated access to Linode's SSH console with optional two-factor authentication (2FA)

Built reproducible local development environments, first with Vagrant and SaltStack, then with Docker Compose, moving the whole stack off physical servers so anyone in the company could contribute; one support engineer who started contributing this way became one of the team's best developers
Championed and implemented the OpenAPI 3 specification for Linode API v4
Managed Jenkins continuous integration (CI) with GitHub Enterprise for automated testing and code quality checks
printHighlights: Built Linode's OAuth 2.0 platform: SSO for its apps, a third-party OAuth provider, and SSH console login with 2FA
Built reproducible local dev environments with Vagrant and Docker Compose, opening contributions company-wide

work.name: Mitel (formerly Ulticom, Inc.)
highlights: Developed a distributed, fault-tolerant Diameter Signaling Controller on Cisco's NCS platform, integrating MongoDB for dynamic routing rules
Built its SOAP and REST APIs with Apache CXF and Jersey, hosted on an embedded Jetty server
Built a metrics collection system for observability with MySQL, Hibernate, and Protocol Buffers

work.name: Amazon.com
highlights: Developed an IP reputation system for Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) with Spring, Hibernate, and Amazon RDS
Built email deliverability monitoring that tracked the reputation of Amazon's mail transfer agents (MTAs) by detecting when mail providers marked messages as junk

projects.name: Nixstasis
projects.description: Self-hosted IoT fleet monitoring and remote device access, no inbound ports.
highlights: Contract-enforced client/server E2E test harness
Remote SSH through lease-bound tunnel credentials, a sandboxed Starlark scripting system, and command allowlist policies
Releases ship .deb, .rpm, and .run packages and container images from CI, with a Docusaurus site for docs and product pages
printHighlights: Remote SSH via lease-bound tunnel credentials; CI-built .deb/.rpm packages and container images

projects.name: AtomixOS
projects.description: NixOS for single-board computers with atomic A/B system updates and automatic rollback.
highlights: Signed RAUC bundles, U-Boot boot-count rollback, a read-only root, and Podman app deployment
38 NixOS VM integration tests, including power-loss and watchdog-rollback scenarios, on Linux and macOS
printHighlights: Signed RAUC bundles; 38 VM tests incl. power-loss and watchdog rollback

projects.name: container-krun-runtime
projects.description: libkrun virtualization runtime for Apple's container; reclaims freed memory for macOS.
highlights: Feature parity for exec, volumes, virtio-fs, and port forwarding, plus memory the guest frees going back to macOS while it runs
Built a native vmnet virtio-net backend in libkrun (Rust) with packed rings, multiqueue TX, and batched syscalls
printHighlights: Built a native vmnet virtio-net backend in libkrun (Rust)

projects.name: container-compose-plugin
projects.description: Unmodified Docker Compose for Apple's container CLI.
highlights: Ports mirrored to localhost and a Docker socket for IDEs and Testcontainers
Built as an external plugin after Apple declined the upstream change
printHighlights: Docker socket for IDEs and Testcontainers; distributed through Homebrew

projects.name: HexBox
projects.description: On-demand ARM64 Linux Nix builder for nix-darwin, in Apple's container.
highlights: 27 releases to v1.2, with idle auto-shutdown and a persistent store
Weekly image rebuilds gated on a 7-day release age, and bot-driven dependency updates
printHighlights: 27 releases to v1.2; weekly image rebuilds gated on 7-day release age

projects.name: Open-source contributions
projects.description: Fixes in docker-library/python, mise, libkrun, and paho-mqtt.
highlights: docker-library/python (official image, 9B+ pulls): found and fixed a silent regression that skipped profile-guided optimization across 37 Dockerfile variants
jdx/mise: OS/architecture compound filters for tool installs
libkrun: released leaked vsock proxies after a clean guest shutdown
eclipse-paho/paho.mqtt.python, Himmelblau, and aube: reconnect and packaging fixes

libkrun: fixed vsock proxy resource leaks on clean shutdown

kept arm64 release builds compatible with glibc 2.31, so they still run on older Debian and Ubuntu

added aarch64 packages for Debian-based distributions
